notes_for_sme: Every row's `type` = 'mcq' (matches the DB canonical, not the analysis label 'simple_mcq').
`marks_correct` = 2, `marks_wrong` = 0.66 across the batch, matching the existing seed questions and BPSC's 1/3 negative-marking convention.

`options` is a jsonb array of {body, isCorrect} objects — the one correct option has isCorrect: true, others false. Matches the exact live schema used by the 8 existing rows and by generate.js's matchesCell().

`concept_group_id` uses human-readable slugs (schema is `text`, not uuid) so an SME can eyeball duplicates during review. Each slug is unique within this batch. If a later batch re-tests the same underlying fact, reuse the slug.

None of the 108 slugs collide with the one existing History fact in the live bank (Non-Cooperation Movement launch year, 1920). Q hb01-007 references the same movement's Chauri Chaura withdrawal — a distinct concept, kept as a separate slug.
`source_citation` names the source type/author rather than quoting — no verbatim external text was copied.
Every question is `status: draft`. Do NOT bulk-import with status='published'. An SME must verify each answer before promotion.
flagged_for_extra_review: hb01-014 (Modern medium — Communal Award): question tests the ANNOUNCER (Ramsay MacDonald), a straightforward attribution. If the SME wants a more specific aspect tested (e.g., which groups got separate electorates, or the Poona Pact response that followed), replace with a differently-focused question.
hb01-069 (Ancient medium — Nalanda founder): Kumaragupta I is the standard NCERT-taught founder-patron; some scholarship gives an earlier Gupta emperor. Kept as Kumaragupta I per textbook standard.
corrections_from_initial_meta_delivery: The initial version of `flagged_for_extra_review` had 5 entries; a post-delivery cross-check found 3 pointed to batch_refs whose actual content was unrelated to the flagged concern (a genuine review-list bug I owned and fixed). hb01-041 was tagged 'Deccan Riots' but is Wood's Dispatch; hb01-085 was tagged 'Charter Act 1853' but is Qutbuddin Aibak / 1206; hb01-098 was tagged 'Talikota' but is Independence Date. The topic/difficulty labels on those wrong entries were also wrong. Only hb01-014 and hb01-069 survived verification; the current list above is the corrected, verified set.

Talikota IS drafted in this batch — at hb01-090 (Medieval medium), not hb01-098. That question asks about the coalition (four Deccan Sultanates: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, Bidar), not the 1565 date, so the 'date granularity' concern from the earlier flag list does not actually apply to any drafted question and no flag is preserved for it.
skipped_topics_worth_considering_for_fut: Deccan Riots (1875): considered but not drafted. This batch already covers 5 peasant/tribal uprisings (Indigo hb01-036, Santhal hb01-037, Munda hb01-038, Tebhaga hb01-039, Telangana hb01-040) — a 6th same-cluster question would have been thematically redundant. Recommend adding in a later Modern-medium batch if the SME wants broader peasant-movement coverage.

Charter Act 1853 civil-services / open-competition provision: considered but not drafted. This batch already has Charter Act 1813 at hb01-043 (medium), Charter Act 1833 at hb01-071 (hard), Regulating Act 1773 at hb01-044, and Pitt's India Act 1784 at hb01-072 in the 'constitutional evolution' cluster. Adding a third Charter Act would have been reasonable to hold for a later batch.
instructions_for_bulk_import: 1. SME reviews every row in `questions[]` for factual accuracy, correct answer index, explanation quality.
2. Any row that fails review is either corrected inline (edit body/options/isCorrect/explanation) or removed.

3. Once cleared, generate a bulk-import CSV/JSON using the surviving rows, with fields mapping to public.questions columns 1:1 (subject, topic, type, difficulty, body, options, marks_correct, marks_wrong, explanation, concept_group_id, source_citation, status).
4. Set status = 'draft' initially — a second human pass in the admin panel flips to 'published' after final review.
5. DO NOT invoke this file's contents directly against the live DB without SME sign-off.

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Partition of Bengal, which came into effect in October 1905, was announced by which Viceroy of India?
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon, Viceroy 1899-1905, announced the Partition of Bengal in July 1905 (effective 16 October 1905), ostensibly for administrative convenience but widely seen as an attempt to divide Hindu and Muslim political interests. The partition was annulled in 1911 under Hardinge II.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Who presided over the first session of the Indian National Congress held in December 1885?
questions.explanation: W.C. Bonnerjee presided over the first INC session at Bombay's Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, 28-31 December 1885. A.O. Hume was the organizer, not the president; Dadabhai Naoroji presided over the 1886, 1893, and 1906 sessions.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was concluded between which two political organizations?

options.body: Indian National Congress and Hindu Mahasabha
Indian National Congress and All-India Muslim League
Indian National Congress and Khilafat Committee
All-India Muslim League and Home Rule League

questions.explanation: The Lucknow Pact was a joint scheme of constitutional reforms agreed between the INC and the Muslim League at their December 1916 Lucknow sessions. The INC accepted separate electorates for Muslims in return for League support for self-government demands.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was popularly known as which of the following?
questions.explanation: The Rowlatt Act (Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act) allowed detention without trial and denied habeas corpus; the Indian press and nationalists called it the 'Black Act' or 'Black Bill'. The 'Gagging Act' is a nickname used for the Vernacular Press Act of 1878.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Jallianwala Bagh massacre of 13 April 1919 was ordered by which British officer?
questions.explanation: Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer ordered troops to open fire on an unarmed crowd at Jallianwala Bagh, Amritsar. Michael O'Dwyer was the Lieutenant-Governor of Punjab who approved Dyer's action; he was later assassinated in London by Udham Singh in 1940 in revenge for the massacre.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Hunter Committee Report 1920

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Khilafat Movement in India (1919-24) was led by which pair of brothers?
questions.explanation: Maulana Shaukat Ali and Maulana Muhammad Ali (the Ali brothers) led the Khilafat Movement demanding the preservation of the Ottoman Caliphate. Gandhi merged it with the Non-Cooperation Movement to build Hindu-Muslim unity.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Non-Cooperation Movement was withdrawn by Mahatma Gandhi in February 1922 following the violent incident at which place?
questions.explanation: On 4 February 1922 at Chauri Chaura in Gorakhpur district (UP), a Congress-led procession clashed with police; the mob set fire to the police station killing 22 policemen. Gandhi withdrew the Non-Cooperation Movement citing its violent turn.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Shahid Amin, Event, Metaphor, Memory: Chauri Chaura 1922-1992

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Swaraj Party, formed in 1923 to contest the Legislative Council elections, was founded by which of the following leaders?

options.body: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Bipin Chandra Pal
Lala Lajpat Rai and Madan Mohan Malaviya
Subhas Chandra Bose and Jawaharlal Nehru

questions.explanation: The Swaraj Party was founded on 1 January 1923 by Motilal Nehru and Chittaranjan (C.R.) Das after they disagreed with the 'no-changer' faction and wanted to enter the legislatures to wreck British administration from within.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Simon Commission was greeted with black-flag demonstrations across India in 1928 primarily because

options.body: it was headed by a Labour Party politician
it did not include any Indian member
it was appointed in secrecy without notifying the Viceroy

questions.explanation: The Indian Statutory Commission (Simon Commission) was an all-white body appointed to review the Government of India Act 1919. The exclusion of Indian members was seen as a national insult, prompting the 'Simon Go Back' agitation in which Lala Lajpat Rai was fatally injured (Lahore, October 1928).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Nehru Report of 1928, drafted as an Indian response to the challenge posed by the Secretary of State, was chaired by
questions.explanation: The Nehru Report was drafted by a committee of the All Parties Conference chaired by Motilal Nehru (not Jawaharlal). It demanded dominion status, joint electorates with reserved seats for minorities, and a bill of rights.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: At which session of the Indian National Congress was the Purna Swaraj (complete independence) resolution passed?
questions.explanation: The Purna Swaraj resolution was adopted at the Lahore Session of the INC in December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru. 26 January 1930 was subsequently observed as Purna Swaraj Day — the date later chosen for the Constitution's commencement in 1950.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Gandhi began the Dandi Salt March on 12 March 1930 from which starting point?
questions.explanation: The 240-mile Dandi March began at Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad, on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on the Gujarat coast on 6 April 1930, where Gandhi symbolically broke the Salt Law by picking up a lump of natural salt.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; The Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi

questions.subject: History
questions.body: At the 1931 Karachi Session of the INC, presided over by Sardar Patel, a landmark resolution was adopted on

options.body: Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme
Purna Swaraj as the Congress goal

questions.explanation: The Karachi Session of March 1931 endorsed the Gandhi-Irwin Pact and, more importantly, adopted the Resolution on Fundamental Rights and National Economic Programme drafted by Nehru — the first time an Indian political party set out a comprehensive rights charter and economic vision.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Communal Award of August 1932 was announced by which British Prime Minister?
questions.explanation: The Communal Award was announced by Labour PM Ramsay MacDonald on 16 August 1932. It granted separate electorates to depressed classes, Muslims, Sikhs, Indian Christians, Anglo-Indians and Europeans. Gandhi's fast-unto-death against the depressed-classes separate electorate led to the Poona Pact.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Poona Pact of September 1932 was signed between
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact was signed on 24 September 1932 between Gandhi (representing caste Hindus) and B.R. Ambedkar (representing depressed classes). It replaced the separate electorate for depressed classes with a system of reserved seats within the general electorate.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Ambedkar, What Congress and Gandhi have done to the Untouchables

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The First Round Table Conference was held in London in 1930-31. Which major Indian political party boycotted it?
questions.explanation: The Congress boycotted the First Round Table Conference (Nov 1930 – Jan 1931) because most of its leadership was in jail during the Civil Disobedience Movement. Gandhi attended only the Second Round Table Conference (1931) as sole Congress representative under the Gandhi-Irwin Pact.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed in March 1931 and led directly to

options.body: Congress participation in the Second Round Table Conference

questions.explanation: The Gandhi-Irwin Pact (5 March 1931) suspended the Civil Disobedience Movement, released political prisoners not accused of violence, and secured Congress agreement to attend the Second Round Table Conference. Provincial autonomy came only with the 1935 Act.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Government of India Act, 1935, introduced which of the following major features?

options.body: Provincial autonomy and an All-India Federation (never operationalised)

questions.explanation: The 1935 Act introduced provincial autonomy (implemented 1937) and provided for an All-India Federation of British Provinces and Princely States — the federal part never came into force because most princely states did not accede. It expanded the franchise but nowhere near universal adult.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The August Offer of 1940 was made by which Viceroy of India?
questions.explanation: Viceroy Linlithgow made the August Offer on 8 August 1940, proposing dominion status after the war, an expanded Executive Council, and a war advisory council. Congress rejected it; the League welcomed the veto-like assurance to minorities.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Cripps Mission was sent to India in March 1942 with proposals that included

options.body: Post-war dominion status with the right of provinces to secede
Formation of a Constituent Assembly by universal adult franchise
Direct transfer of power to Congress and League

questions.explanation: Sir Stafford Cripps offered dominion status after the war and the right of any province to opt out (a Pakistan seed). Gandhi called it a 'post-dated cheque on a crashing bank'. Congress rejected the proposals, leading to the Quit India resolution in August 1942.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Quit India Resolution was passed by the AICC at its session held in
questions.explanation: The AICC passed the Quit India Resolution at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, on 8 August 1942 — the venue is now called August Kranti Maidan. Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' call the same evening; mass arrests followed on 9 August.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Who was the founder-leader of the Indian National Army (Azad Hind Fauj) before Subhas Chandra Bose took charge in 1943?
questions.explanation: Captain Mohan Singh formed the first INA from Indian PoWs in Malaya in 1942; it was later re-organized under the Indian Independence League led by Rash Behari Bose, who handed leadership to Subhas Chandra Bose in Singapore on 4 July 1943.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Peter Ward Fay, The Forgotten Army

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Cabinet Mission that came to India in March 1946 consisted of which three British ministers?
questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission comprised Secretary of State Lord Pethick-Lawrence (chair), Sir Stafford Cripps, and First Lord of the Admiralty A.V. Alexander. It rejected the demand for Pakistan and proposed a three-tier federal structure with a Constituent Assembly.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: 'Direct Action Day' was observed by the All-India Muslim League on which date?
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ali Jinnah declared 16 August 1946 as Direct Action Day to press the demand for Pakistan after the League rejected the Cabinet Mission's interim government arrangement. It triggered the 'Great Calcutta Killings' — communal violence that spread to Noakhali, Bihar, and beyond.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Mountbatten Plan for partition of British India was announced on
questions.explanation: Viceroy Lord Mountbatten announced the partition plan (also called the 3 June Plan) on 3 June 1947, providing for the creation of India and Pakistan as separate dominions. The 20 February 1947 statement by PM Attlee had earlier promised transfer of power by June 1948.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Bal Gangadhar Tilak founded his Home Rule League in April 1916 with its headquarters at
questions.explanation: Tilak's Indian Home Rule League was set up at Belgaum in April 1916 with headquarters at Poona; it worked mainly in Maharashtra, Karnataka, the Central Provinces and Berar. Annie Besant's parallel All-India Home Rule League (September 1916) had its headquarters at Madras and worked in the rest of India.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Ghadar Party, founded in 1913 to overthrow British rule in India by armed revolt, was headquartered in which city?
questions.explanation: The Ghadar Party (Hindi Association of the Pacific Coast) was founded in San Francisco in 1913 by Lala Har Dayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, and others. Its weekly paper 'Ghadar' was published from the Yugantar Ashram at San Francisco in multiple Indian languages.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Harish K. Puri, Ghadar Movement: Ideology, Organisation & Strategy

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Kakori Train Robbery of 9 August 1925 was organized by which revolutionary organization?
questions.explanation: The Kakori conspiracy — the looting of a train carrying government treasury near Kakori (UP) — was executed by the Hindustan Republican Association (HRA) led by Ram Prasad Bismil, Ashfaqullah Khan, Rajendra Lahiri and others. The HRA was renamed Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) in 1928.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: On 8 April 1929, Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt threw bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly primarily to protest against

options.body: The Public Safety Bill and Trade Disputes Bill

questions.explanation: Bhagat Singh and B.K. Dutt threw non-lethal bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly to protest the Public Safety Bill and the Trade Disputes Bill, chanting 'Inquilab Zindabad'. They deliberately courted arrest to use the trial as a platform.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Kuldip Nayar, The Martyr: Bhagat Singh

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Hindustan Socialist Republican Association (HSRA) was formally founded in September 1928 at
questions.explanation: The HSRA was founded at a meeting held at Ferozeshah Kotla ground in Delhi on 8-9 September 1928, adding 'Socialist' to the earlier HRA name at the instance of Bhagat Singh and his comrades to declare a broader social objective.
questions.source_citation: Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence; Chaman Lal, Bhagat Singh Reader

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Vernacular Press Act was enacted in 1878 by which Viceroy?
questions.explanation: The Vernacular Press Act was passed by Lord Lytton in 1878 to muzzle Indian-language newspapers criticising British policy. Popularly called the 'Gagging Act', it was repealed by Lord Ripon in 1882.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Ilbert Bill controversy of 1883-84 concerned

options.body: The right of Indian judges to try Europeans in criminal cases
Separation of the judiciary from the executive
Introduction of jury trials in mofussil courts
The abolition of the Presidency Small Cause Courts

questions.explanation: Introduced under Viceroy Ripon by law member C.P. Ilbert, the Bill proposed to allow Indian judges/magistrates to try European British subjects in criminal cases in the mofussil. Vehement European opposition forced a compromise version restricting the right.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Age of Consent Act, 1891, raised the minimum age of marriage for girls in India from 10 years to
questions.explanation: The Age of Consent Act of 1891, pushed by Behramji Malabari, raised the age of consent (effectively minimum marriageable age for consummation) from 10 to 12 years. It provoked heated opposition from orthodox opinion, notably Tilak.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The abolition of Sati was enacted in 1829 by Regulation XVII under which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: Governor-General Lord William Bentinck passed Regulation XVII of 1829 declaring Sati (the burning of widows) a criminal offence, initially in Bengal Presidency and later extended. Raja Rammohan Roy's advocacy was central to the reform.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act, 1856, was passed during the Governor-Generalship of
questions.explanation: The Hindu Widow Remarriage Act was passed on 25 July 1856 during the Governor-Generalship of Lord Dalhousie, largely due to the efforts of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar. It legalised remarriage of Hindu widows.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 primarily broke out in which region?
questions.explanation: The Indigo Revolt of 1859-60 was a peasant uprising in Bengal — Nadia, Jessore, Pabna, Malda and neighbouring districts — against planters who forced cultivation of indigo. Champaran was Gandhi's later 1917 Satyagraha against the same tinkathia system.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Ranajit Guha, Elementary Aspects of Peasant Insurgency

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Santhal Rebellion (Hool) of 1855-56 against the British and local moneylenders was led primarily by
questions.explanation: The Santhal Hool of 30 June 1855 was led by brothers Sidhu and Kanhu Murmu (with Chand and Bhairav) against zamindars, mahajans and British authority in the Damin-i-Koh region (present-day Jharkhand). It was brutally suppressed by 1856.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Munda Uprising (Ulgulan) of 1899-1900 against British rule was led by
questions.explanation: Birsa Munda led the Ulgulan (Great Tumult) among the Munda tribals of Chotanagpur against dikus (outsiders), zamindars and Christian missionaries, demanding restoration of tribal land rights (khuntkatti). He died in Ranchi jail in June 1900.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; K.S. Singh, Birsa Munda and His Movement

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Tebhaga peasant movement of 1946-47, which demanded that the sharecropper's share be raised to two-thirds of the produce, took place mainly in
questions.explanation: The Tebhaga (literally 'three shares') movement was led by the Kisan Sabha in Bengal (largely North Bengal) in 1946-47, demanding that bargadars (sharecroppers) retain two-thirds instead of one-half of the harvest, based on the Floud Commission recommendation.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Telangana peasant armed struggle (1946-51) was primarily directed against

options.body: The Nizam of Hyderabad and jagirdari-deshmukh landlords

questions.explanation: The Telangana armed struggle, led by the Andhra Mahasabha and the Communist Party of India, mobilised peasants against the Nizam's autocratic rule and the exploitative jagirdari-deshmukh-vetti (forced labour) system. It continued after Hyderabad's accession (1948) until 1951.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Sundarayya, Telangana People's Struggle and Its Lessons

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Wood's Educational Dispatch, considered the 'Magna Carta of English education in India', was issued in
questions.explanation: Sir Charles Wood's Dispatch of July 1854 (during Dalhousie) recommended: English as the medium for higher study, vernaculars for primary; grants-in-aid for private schools; universities at Calcutta, Bombay and Madras (established 1857); and a Department of Public Instruction in each province.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Hunter Commission of 1882 was constituted to review

options.body: Indian education, particularly primary and secondary
The condition of the Indian press

questions.explanation: The 1882 Hunter Commission (chaired by William Hunter) reviewed the progress of Indian education since Wood's Dispatch, focusing on primary and secondary levels. Do not confuse with the 1919-20 Hunter Committee that inquired into the Jallianwala Bagh massacre.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; S.R. Mehrotra, A History of the Indian National Congress

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Charter Act of 1813 marked a turning point in British Indian policy because it

options.body: Ended the East India Company's trading monopoly in India (except tea and trade with China)
Introduced the office of Governor-General of India
Established the Supreme Court at Calcutta

questions.explanation: The Charter Act of 1813 renewed the Company's charter for 20 years but ended its monopoly of trade with India (retaining monopoly of tea and China trade). It also allotted Rs 1 lakh for education and allowed Christian missionaries to enter India.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Regulating Act of 1773 provided for the appointment of the first
questions.explanation: The Regulating Act of 1773 created the office of Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings was the first) with authority over Bombay and Madras Presidencies. The title 'Governor-General of India' was created only by the Charter Act of 1833 (William Bentinck the first).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Doctrine of Lapse, aggressively used to annex Indian princely states in the 1840s-50s, is chiefly associated with
questions.explanation: Governor-General Lord Dalhousie (1848-56) applied the Doctrine of Lapse to annex states including Satara (1848), Jaitpur and Sambalpur (1849), Baghat (1850), Udaipur (1852), Jhansi (1853), and Nagpur (1854), fuelling resentment that contributed to the 1857 Revolt.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Revolt of 1857 first broke out on 10 May 1857 at
questions.explanation: Although Mangal Pandey's earlier defiance at Barrackpore (29 March 1857) is often cited as the spark, the general outbreak occurred at Meerut on 10 May 1857 when sepoys of the 3rd Cavalry rose, marched to Delhi, and proclaimed Bahadur Shah II Emperor of Hindustan.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; R.C. Majumdar, The Sepoy Mutiny and the Revolt of 1857

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Government of India Act, 1858, transferred the administration of India from the East India Company to
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1858 (Queen's Proclamation of 1 November 1858) abolished the East India Company and transferred power to the British Crown. A Secretary of State for India, assisted by a 15-member Council, replaced the Board of Control and Court of Directors.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Indian Councils Act, 1909, is popularly known as the
questions.explanation: The Indian Councils Act of 1909 — after Secretary of State John Morley and Viceroy Lord Minto — expanded legislative councils and introduced separate electorates for Muslims. The Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms were the Government of India Act 1919.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Dyarchy in the provinces was introduced in India by which Act?
questions.explanation: The Government of India Act, 1919 (Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms) introduced dyarchy in the provinces — dividing provincial subjects into Reserved (governed by the Governor and his executive council) and Transferred (governed by ministers responsible to the legislature).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Interim Government of India, formed on 2 September 1946, was headed by
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru was sworn in as Vice-President of the Executive Council (effectively Prime Minister) of the Interim Government on 2 September 1946. The Muslim League joined only on 26 October 1946 with Liaquat Ali Khan in charge of Finance.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Which of the following is NOT a site of the Indus Valley Civilization located in present-day India?
questions.explanation: Mohenjodaro lies in Sindh province of present-day Pakistan (along with Harappa in Punjab, Pakistan). The other three — Lothal, Dholavira, Banawali — are all in present-day India.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Great Bath of the Indus Valley Civilization has been found at
questions.explanation: The Great Bath (approx. 12 m × 7 m, 2.4 m deep, watertight brick construction with bitumen lining) was excavated at Mohenjodaro. Lothal is noted for its dockyard, Kalibangan for its ploughed field and fire altars, and Harappa for its granaries.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Which is the oldest and most sacred of the Vedas?
questions.explanation: The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas, composed roughly between 1500-1000 BCE. It consists of 10 mandalas containing 1028 suktas (hymns). The Samaveda largely draws its verses from the Rigveda set to melody.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past

questions.subject: History
questions.body: How many Mahajanapadas are mentioned in the early Buddhist text 'Anguttara Nikaya'?
questions.explanation: The Anguttara Nikaya lists 16 Mahajanapadas (great states) of the 6th century BCE, including Magadha, Kosala, Vatsa, Avanti, Anga, Kashi, and others. Magadha (with capital Rajgriha, later Pataliputra) eventually absorbed the others.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Romila Thapar, The Penguin History of Early India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The First Buddhist Council was held immediately after the Buddha's death (Mahaparinirvana) at
questions.explanation: The First Buddhist Council was held around 483 BCE at Sattapanni cave, Rajgriha (Rajgir, Bihar) under the patronage of Ajatashatru, presided over by Mahakassapa. Sutta and Vinaya Pitakas were compiled. Later councils met at Vaishali (2nd), Pataliputra (3rd), Kundalvana (4th).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Romila Thapar, The Penguin History of Early India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Ashoka's Kalinga War, after which he embraced Buddhism, is dated to approximately
questions.explanation: The Kalinga War is dated to c. 261 BCE, the 8th regnal year of Ashoka. Rock Edict XIII describes his remorse at the loss of life and his subsequent adoption of Dhamma. 232 BCE is his approximate death year; the Mauryan dynasty ended c. 185 BCE with Brihadratha's assassination.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Romila Thapar, Asoka and the Decline of the Mauryas

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The 'Arthashastra', a foundational text on statecraft and political economy, is attributed to
questions.explanation: The Arthashastra is attributed to Kautilya (also called Chanakya or Vishnugupta), traditionally the chief minister of Chandragupta Maurya. It covers administration, taxation, law, diplomacy and military strategy. The extant recension was rediscovered by R. Shamasastry in 1905.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Kautilya, Arthashastra (tr. R.P. Kangle)

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The founder of the Sunga dynasty, who assassinated the last Maurya ruler Brihadratha around 185 BCE, was
questions.explanation: Pushyamitra Sunga, commander-in-chief under Brihadratha, killed the emperor and founded the Sunga dynasty c. 185 BCE. He is known for performing Ashvamedha sacrifices and repelling Indo-Greek invasions. Agnimitra was his son (immortalised in Kalidasa's Malavikagnimitram).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Kushana king who is credited with convening the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir was
questions.explanation: Kanishka I (early 2nd century CE) convened the Fourth Buddhist Council at Kundalvana in Kashmir under the presidency of Vasumitra (with Ashvaghosha as vice-president). It marked the formal division into Hinayana and Mahayana schools.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Romila Thapar, The Penguin History of Early India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Sangam literature was primarily composed in which language and region?
questions.explanation: The Sangam corpus (c. 300 BCE – 300 CE) comprises Tamil poetry composed under the patronage of the Chera, Chola and Pandya kings of ancient Tamilakam. Tolkappiyam (grammar), the Ettuthogai and Pattupattu anthologies, and the twin epics Silappadikaram and Manimekalai are landmark works.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; K.A. Nilakanta Sastri, A History of South India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Aryabhata, the astronomer-mathematician who proposed the earth's rotation on its axis, lived during the reign of which dynasty?
questions.explanation: Aryabhata (b. 476 CE) composed the Aryabhatiya in 499 CE at Kusumapura (Pataliputra) during the Gupta age. He explained lunar and solar eclipses scientifically and proposed that the earth's daily rotation causes the apparent movement of the stars.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Romila Thapar, The Penguin History of Early India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Harshavardhana ruled from his capital at
questions.explanation: Harsha (r. 606-647 CE) initially ruled from Thanesar (Sthanvishvara), his family's original seat, but shifted his capital to Kanauj (Kanyakubja) after ascending to the throne of Kanauj (his sister Rajyashri's kingdom).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Bana, Harshacharita; Hsuan Tsang, Si-Yu-Ki

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Chinese pilgrim Hsuan Tsang (Xuanzang), who spent about 13 years in India, visited during the reign of
questions.explanation: Hsuan Tsang travelled through India c. 630-644 CE during Harshavardhana's reign. His account 'Si-Yu-Ki' (Records of the Western Regions) is a major source for 7th-century Indian society and Nalanda University. Fa-Hien had visited earlier, during Chandragupta II's reign.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Hsuan Tsang, Si-Yu-Ki

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The founder of the Nanda dynasty of Magadha, who preceded the Mauryas, was
questions.explanation: Mahapadma Nanda (r. c. 345 BCE onwards) founded the Nanda dynasty, described in the Puranas as 'sarva-kshatrantaka' (destroyer of all Kshatriyas). His son Dhana Nanda, the last Nanda, was overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya c. 321 BCE.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; R.S. Sharma, India's Ancient Past

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Which Chola king is credited with launching a successful naval expedition against Srivijaya (a maritime empire in Southeast Asia) in the 11th century?
questions.explanation: Rajendra Chola I (r. 1014-1044 CE) launched a naval expedition against the Srivijaya empire (based in Sumatra) around 1025 CE. He also assumed the title 'Gangaikonda Chola' after his northern campaign to the Ganga.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; K.A. Nilakanta Sastri, The Colas

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Kailasa temple at Ellora, an architectural marvel carved out of a single rock, was constructed under the patronage of which dynasty?
questions.explanation: The Kailasa temple (Cave 16 at Ellora) was commissioned by Rashtrakuta king Krishna I (r. c. 756-773 CE). It is a monolithic rock-cut structure carved top-down from a single basalt hill, dedicated to Shiva.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; A.L. Basham, The Wonder That Was India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Which Gupta ruler assumed the title 'Vikramaditya' and is traditionally credited with defeating the Western Kshatrapas (Sakas)?
questions.explanation: Chandragupta II (r. c. 375-415 CE) assumed the title Vikramaditya after his victory over the Western Kshatrapas (Sakas) of Malwa and Kathiawar, extending Gupta rule to the western coast. The court of the Nine Gems (Navaratnas), including Kalidasa, is traditionally associated with him.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Romila Thapar, The Penguin History of Early India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Which Ashokan edict describes the horrors of the Kalinga War and the emperor's remorse?
questions.explanation: Major Rock Edict XIII (found at Shahbazgarhi, Mansehra, Kalsi, Girnar, Erragudi, but notably NOT at any Kalinga site) records Ashoka's remorse after the Kalinga War, the death and captivity figures, and his turn to Dhamma-vijaya (conquest by righteousness).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; D.C. Sircar, Inscriptions of Asoka

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Nalanda Mahavihara, the celebrated ancient centre of learning in Bihar, was founded by
questions.explanation: Nalanda is generally traced to the Gupta emperor Kumaragupta I (r. c. 415-455 CE) as its founder-patron. It flourished under subsequent Gupta rulers and Harshavardhana, and continued under the Palas (Dharmapala expanded it) until its destruction by Bakhtiyar Khilji c. 1193.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Ancient India; Romila Thapar, The Penguin History of Early India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Dadabhai Naoroji's 'Drain of Wealth' theory was most systematically expounded in his book

options.body: Poverty and Un-British Rule in India

questions.explanation: Dadabhai Naoroji's 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India' (1901) is the classic statement of the Drain theory, showing that a steady, one-way transfer of Indian wealth to Britain was the root cause of Indian poverty. Romesh Chandra Dutt's 'Economic History of India' (1902, 1904) is a related but distinct work.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, The Rise and Growth of Economic Nationalism in India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Charter Act of 1833 abolished the East India Company's monopoly of which of the following trades?

options.body: Trade with China (the last remaining monopoly)
Trade in salt and opium within India

questions.explanation: The 1813 Act had ended the Company's Indian trade monopoly but kept its China trade and tea monopoly. The Charter Act of 1833 ended these last commercial privileges, making the Company a purely administrative body. The Act also created the office of Governor-General of India (Bentinck the first).
questions.source_citation: Bipin Chandra, Modern India; Ram Chandra Guha, India After Gandhi (background chapters)

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Pitt's India Act of 1784 established which body to exercise supervisory control over the East India Company's affairs on behalf of the British government?
questions.explanation: Pitt's India Act, 1784, created a six-member Board of Control (British government appointees) alongside the Company's Court of Directors, establishing dual government of India. The Board of Control was abolished by the Government of India Act, 1858, replaced by the Secretary of State for India.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Third Anglo-Maratha War (1817-18) resulted in

options.body: The formal end of the Maratha Confederacy and the Peshwaship
The signing of the Treaty of Bassein
British acquisition of Malwa but no political change

questions.explanation: The Third Anglo-Maratha War (also called the Pindari War), 1817-18, was fought under Lord Hastings. It ended with the defeat of Peshwa Baji Rao II, the formal abolition of the Peshwaship, and the annexation of Peshwa's territories to the Bombay Presidency. The Treaty of Bassein (1802) had preceded the Second War.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Battle of Buxar (1764) was fought between the British East India Company and a combined force of

options.body: Siraj-ud-Daulah, Awadh Nawab, and Mughal Emperor
Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daulah of Awadh, and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II
Tipu Sultan, the Marathas, and the Nizam
Mir Jafar, Nawab of Bengal, and the French

questions.explanation: At Buxar (22 October 1764), Hector Munro's British force defeated the combined army of Mir Qasim (ousted Nawab of Bengal), Shuja-ud-Daulah (Nawab of Awadh), and Mughal Emperor Shah Alam II. The Treaty of Allahabad (1765) followed, granting the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Second Anglo-Sikh War (1848-49) ended with the annexation of Punjab under which Governor-General?
questions.explanation: The Second Anglo-Sikh War ended with the Battle of Gujrat (February 1849). Governor-General Lord Dalhousie annexed the Punjab in March 1849 and set up the Board of Administration (three-man board including the Lawrence brothers) to govern it.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Vellore Mutiny of July 1806 by sepoys was triggered primarily by

options.body: A new pay scale that reduced allowances
Regulations changing sepoys' turban, beard and religious markings
Recruitment of low-caste soldiers into the same regiments

questions.explanation: The immediate cause of the Vellore Mutiny (10 July 1806) was General John Cradock's order changing the sepoys' headgear (round hat like Europeans), banning caste marks, and prohibiting beards — perceived as forced Christianisation. About 100 British and around 350 sepoys died before the mutiny was suppressed.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Rampa Rebellion of 1922-24 in the Godavari Agency of the Madras Presidency was led by
questions.explanation: Alluri Sitarama Raju led the Rampa (Manyam) Rebellion of Koya tribals in the Godavari Agency against the 1882 Madras Forest Act's restrictions on shifting cultivation and the exploitative muttadari system. He was captured and executed in May 1924.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; David Arnold, The Congress in Tamilnad

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The 'Deoband Movement', a revivalist Islamic educational movement, was founded in 1867 by

options.body: Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi

questions.explanation: The Darul Uloom at Deoband (Saharanpur district, UP) was founded in 1867 by Muhammad Qasim Nanautavi and Rashid Ahmad Gangohi as a traditionalist counterpoint to Aligarh-style modernism. Its scholars generally supported the Congress-led nationalist movement.
questions.source_citation: Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence; Barbara Metcalf, Islamic Revival in British India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Muzaffarpur bomb (30 April 1908) that killed Mrs and Miss Kennedy — intended for the judge Douglas Kingsford — was thrown by
questions.explanation: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki, members of Anushilan Samiti, threw a bomb at what they believed was Kingsford's carriage in Muzaffarpur on 30 April 1908; two English ladies (Mrs and Miss Kennedy) were killed. Chaki committed suicide when cornered; Khudiram was hanged on 11 August 1908 at Muzaffarpur jail.
questions.source_citation: Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947; Peter Heehs, The Bomb in Bengal

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Which of the following was NOT part of the Cabinet Mission Plan (1946)?

options.body: Grouping of provinces into three sections
An interim government at the Centre
A separate Constituent Assembly for Muslim-majority provinces

questions.explanation: The Cabinet Mission Plan explicitly rejected a separate Pakistan/Constituent Assembly for Muslim-majority provinces. It proposed a united India with three sections (A: Hindu-majority, B: Muslim-majority NW, C: Bengal+Assam), a three-tier federation, and a single Constituent Assembly. The rejection of Pakistan is precisely why the League later launched Direct Action.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The 'Servants of India Society', founded in 1905 for training national workers, was established by
questions.explanation: Gopal Krishna Gokhale founded the Servants of India Society in Pune on 12 June 1905. Its members took vows of poverty, and worked on famine relief, education for the depressed classes, and constitutional agitation. Gokhale was Gandhi's political guru.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Butler Committee (1927-28) was constituted to examine

options.body: Financial relations between the Centre and provinces
Relations between the Indian Princely States and the British Crown
The working of dyarchy in the provinces
The rights of Indians in South Africa

questions.explanation: The Indian States Committee (Butler Committee), chaired by Sir Harcourt Butler, examined relations between the British Crown and the Princely States. It reported in 1929 that paramountcy resided in the Crown, not the British Parliament — an issue that became central during the federation debate under the 1935 Act.
questions.source_citation: Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence; Sumit Sarkar, Modern India 1885-1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Wahabi Movement in 19th-century India was politically active mainly in

options.body: Bengal, Bihar and the North-West Frontier

questions.explanation: Inspired by Sayyid Ahmad of Rai Bareilly (killed at Balakot, 1831), the Wahabi (Tariqah-i-Muhammadiya) movement drew recruits and organisational strength from Bengal (Patna as a key centre), Bihar, and the North-West Frontier, mounting armed resistance against Sikh and later British power until the 1870s.
questions.source_citation: Bipin Chandra, Modern India; Qeyamuddin Ahmad, The Wahabi Movement in India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The 'August Kranti' (August Revolution) of 1942 was directly triggered by which event?

options.body: The arrest of Congress leaders on 9 August 1942

questions.explanation: On the night of 8-9 August 1942, immediately after the Quit India resolution, the British arrested the entire top Congress leadership (Operation Zero Hour). The absence of central direction triggered a spontaneous mass upsurge — the 'August Kranti' — with strikes, sabotage of communications, and parallel governments established at places like Ballia, Tamluk and Satara.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Delhi Sultanate began with the accession of which ruler as Sultan in 1206?
questions.explanation: Qutbuddin Aibak, a slave-general of Muhammad of Ghor, ascended as Sultan in 1206 at Lahore after Muhammad Ghori's death, founding the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty. He is popularly known for beginning construction of the Qutb Minar and the Quwwat-ul-Islam Mosque at Delhi.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part I

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Iltutmish is regarded as the 'real founder' of the Delhi Sultanate primarily because

options.body: He was the first Turkic ruler in India
He organised its administration, currency and territorial base, and obtained Caliphate recognition
He defeated the Mongols in a major battle

questions.explanation: Iltutmish (r. 1211-1236) organised the iqta system, introduced the silver tanka and copper jital, established the Turkan-i-Chihalgani ('The Forty' nobles), moved the capital firmly to Delhi, and obtained a formal patent from the Abbasid Caliph in 1229 — actions that consolidated the Sultanate as a state.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part I

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Alauddin Khilji's market reforms fixed the prices of

options.body: Essential commodities including grain, cloth, cattle and slaves

questions.explanation: Alauddin Khilji (r. 1296-1316) fixed the prices of a wide range of essential commodities — grains (in Mandi), cloth (in Sarai Adl), cattle, horses and slaves — under a rigorous system of state control with dedicated market officers (Diwan-i-Riyasat, Shahna-i-Mandi) to sustain his standing army and check hoarding.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part I

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Muhammad bin Tughlaq introduced token currency of copper and brass around 1329-30. It failed primarily because

options.body: The nobles refused to accept it
The state did not monopolise minting, allowing widespread forgery
There was no shortage of silver in the treasury

questions.explanation: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token coins (copper/brass with silver value) failed because the state did not enforce a mint monopoly — private minting flourished, forgeries flooded the market, and foreign traders refused the tokens. He eventually withdrew them and redeemed all tokens (genuine or forged) in silver, draining the treasury.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part I

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The founder of the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336 CE were

options.body: Deva Raya I and Deva Raya II

questions.explanation: Harihara I and Bukka I, the Sangama brothers, founded the Vijayanagara Empire on the south bank of the Tungabhadra in 1336 CE, initially with the guidance of the sage Vidyaranya. Their capital, Vijayanagara (present-day Hampi), grew into a major medieval South Indian empire.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Battle of Talikota in 1565, which decisively weakened the Vijayanagara Empire, was fought against a coalition of

options.body: Four Deccan Sultanates: Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda and Bidar

questions.explanation: At Talikota (also called the Battle of Rakshasa-Tangdi) in January 1565, Vijayanagara under Rama Raya was defeated by a confederation of the four Deccan Sultanates — Bijapur, Ahmadnagar, Golconda, and Bidar (Berar largely stayed neutral). The city of Vijayanagara was sacked, and the empire declined rapidly thereafter.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Bahmani Sultanate was founded in 1347 by
questions.explanation: Alauddin Hasan Bahman Shah (also known as Hasan Gangu), an Afghan noble in the Deccan, revolted against Muhammad bin Tughlaq and founded the Bahmani Sultanate at Daulatabad in 1347, later shifting the capital to Gulbarga and then Bidar.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Shivaji's council of eight ministers is known as
questions.explanation: Shivaji, after his coronation in 1674 at Raigad, organised his administration around the Ashta Pradhan — a council of eight ministers including the Peshwa (PM), Amatya (finance), Sachiv (secretary), Mantri (record-keeper), Senapati (military), Sumant (foreign), Nyayadhish (justice) and Panditrao (religion/charities).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Akbar's revenue system, known as the Dahsala or Zabti system (finalised c. 1580), was primarily designed by
questions.explanation: Raja Todar Mal, Akbar's Finance Minister (Diwan-i-Ashraf), finalised the Dahsala system c. 1580: assessment was based on average produce and prices over the preceding ten years, and revenue was fixed in cash. It applied to the standard subas (provinces) — the core of Akbar's fiscal machinery.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II; Abul Fazl, Ain-i-Akbari

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Mughal mansabdari system introduced by Akbar assigned each noble two ranks. What did these two ranks represent?

options.body: Zat (personal rank/status) and Sawar (cavalry contingent to be maintained)

questions.explanation: Every mansabdar held a Zat (which fixed personal status, pay, and place at court) and a Sawar (which fixed the number of cavalrymen he had to maintain). The zat-sawar combination determined the noble's obligations and rewards, and the system was refined by later Mughals into du-aspa/sih-aspa categories.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Guru Gobind Singh established the Khalsa Panth in the year
questions.explanation: On Baisakhi day, 13 April 1699, at Anandpur Sahib, Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa — a community of the initiated (Amrit-dhari) — beginning with the Panj Pyare (Five Beloved Ones). He was the tenth and last human Sikh Guru; before his death in 1708, he vested Guruship in the Guru Granth Sahib.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; J.S. Grewal, The Sikhs of the Punjab

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Bhakti saint Kabir was primarily associated with which tradition?

options.body: Nirguna Bhakti (worship of a formless divine)

questions.explanation: Kabir (15th century, Varanasi), a weaver by profession, belonged to the Nirguna Bhakti tradition — worship of a formless, attributeless divine. His verses (dohas), collected in the Bijak, blended Hindu and Islamic ideas and are also included in the Guru Granth Sahib. Saguna Bhakti was represented by figures like Tulsidas and Mira.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Medieval India; Satish Chandra, Medieval India Part II

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Who wrote the national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.explanation: 'Jana Gana Mana' was written in Bengali by Rabindranath Tagore in 1911 and first sung at the Calcutta session of the INC on 27 December 1911. It was adopted as the national anthem by the Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950. Bankim Chandra wrote 'Vande Mataram' (national song).
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Constituent Assembly Debates, Volume XII

questions.subject: History
questions.body: India gained independence from British rule on
questions.explanation: India gained independence at midnight on 14-15 August 1947 under the Indian Independence Act, 1947. 26 January 1950 is Republic Day (Constitution came into force). 14 August 1947 is Pakistan's Independence Day.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Indian Independence Act, 1947

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The first Prime Minister of independent India was
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru took the oath as India's first Prime Minister on 15 August 1947 and served until his death on 27 May 1964. Rajendra Prasad became the first President (of the Republic) in 1950; Vallabhbhai Patel was Deputy PM and Home Minister.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Ramachandra Guha, India After Gandhi

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Vallabhbhai Patel is popularly known as the
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is called the 'Iron Man of India' (or 'Sardar' / 'Loh Purush') for his role as first Home Minister in integrating over 560 princely states into the Indian Union. 'Father of the Nation' is Mahatma Gandhi; 'Lokmanya' is Tilak; 'Netaji' is Subhas Chandra Bose.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Rajmohan Gandhi, Patel: A Life

questions.subject: History
questions.body: Mahatma Gandhi is known as the 'Father of the Nation' in India. Who is said to have first addressed him by this title in a radio broadcast?
questions.explanation: Subhas Chandra Bose, in his Azad Hind Radio address from Singapore on 6 July 1944, addressed Gandhi as 'Father of the Nation' while seeking his blessings for the INA's final push. The title later became universal.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Peter Ward Fay, The Forgotten Army

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Indian National Congress was founded in the year
questions.explanation: The Indian National Congress was founded at Bombay on 28 December 1885 under the presidency of W.C. Bonnerjee, with A.O. Hume as the organizing secretary. 72 delegates from across British India attended the first session.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, India's Struggle for Independence

questions.subject: History
questions.body: 'Vande Mataram', later adopted as the national song, was written by
questions.explanation: 'Vande Mataram' was composed by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and included in his 1882 novel 'Anandamath'. The Constituent Assembly on 24 January 1950 accorded it equal status with the national anthem 'Jana Gana Mana', declaring it the national song.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Constituent Assembly Debates, Volume XII

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Ramakrishna Mission was founded in 1897 by
questions.explanation: Swami Vivekananda (Narendranath Datta, 1863-1902) founded the Ramakrishna Mission on 1 May 1897 at Belur Math, near Calcutta, after his return from the World's Parliament of Religions at Chicago (1893). It combines Vedantic teaching with social service.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Bipin Chandra, Modern India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Cellular Jail, used by the British to imprison many Indian freedom fighters, is located in
questions.explanation: The Cellular Jail ('Kala Pani') at Port Blair, Andaman and Nicobar Islands, was completed in 1906 and used for solitary confinement of political prisoners including V.D. Savarkar, Batukeshwar Dutt, and hundreds of revolutionaries. It is now a national memorial.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Ministry of Culture, Government of India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The slogan 'Do or Die' was given by Mahatma Gandhi at the launch of which movement?
questions.explanation: Gandhi gave the 'Karo ya Maro' (Do or Die) call at Gowalia Tank Maidan, Bombay, on 8 August 1942, immediately after the Quit India resolution — asking Indians to either free India or die trying.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Collected Works of Mahatma Gandhi, Vol. 76

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The book 'The Discovery of India' was written by
questions.explanation: Jawaharlal Nehru wrote 'The Discovery of India' during his imprisonment at Ahmednagar Fort (1942-46). It surveys Indian civilization from ancient to modern times. Gandhi's autobiography is 'The Story of My Experiments with Truth'.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Jawaharlal Nehru, The Discovery of India

questions.subject: History
questions.body: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, Mahatma Gandhi's first major experiment with Satyagraha in India, was launched in support of

options.body: Peasants oppressed under the tinkathia (indigo) system

questions.explanation: Champaran Satyagraha (April 1917) mobilised peasants of Champaran district in Bihar against the tinkathia system, under which planters compelled peasants to grow indigo on 3/20 of their land. Raj Kumar Shukla persuaded Gandhi to visit. The Champaran Agrarian Committee (1917) led to the Champaran Agrarian Act (1918) abolishing tinkathia.
questions.source_citation: NCERT Modern India; Rajendra Prasad, Champaran Satyagraha
